pass_a_gloss: [...] to a people who will not profit them, neither for help nor for profit, but for shame and reproach. He laments again over those from Israel as lovers of sin and having become apostates, very wicked and planning bitter things, not through God. For indeed it is not lawful that those wishing to be of one mind upon some of the base things take counsel with God. But everyone who is pious and good and a lover of righteousness will take counsel with God and will advance toward the things to be done. For it is written that: Thoughts of righteous are judgments. He accuses then the chosen Israel, as having brought in a mind discordant with God regarding Christ. For they were considering, sitting in council, and indeed were saying: What are we doing, because this man does many signs? If we let him thus, the Romans will come and will take away both your city and the country. And another one of those set among leaders, You, he says, know nothing, that it is profitable that one man die, and not the whole nation perish. More clearly the Lord teaches this very thing, saying in gospel parables that: The master of the house who planted the vineyard sent his own slaves so as to receive the fruits, but the farmers killed these. And not as far as these did the charges of their impiety come; but indeed having beheld also the son sent by the father after the household servants, they said, it says, among themselves: This is the heir, come, let us kill him and have for ourselves his inheritance. Apostates therefore are the introducers of such bitter and unholy schemes, those adding sin upon sins; for they killed, as I said, holy prophets; then also after those the heir himself, that is, the son. And that from long before their mind looks toward the apostasy from God, he tries to give full assurance, saying: Those going to go down into Egypt; but me they did not ask, to be helped by Pharaoh, and to be sheltered by Egyptians. He threw in through the middle the 'But me they did not ask'. And the sequence of the thoughts has this manner: Woe, he says, those going down into Egypt to be helped by Pharaoh, and to find shelter, that from the Egyptians. For war and battle having been announced to them, and the king of Assyria having moved weapons against the country of the Jews, they ran ahead to the Egyptians, and were calling the help from them, although it was needed to appease God, and to wipe off by the turnings toward the better things the things in which they had offended him. For being rich with the favour from him, they would not have been brought under the feet of those making war [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: …“to a people who will not profit them, neither for help nor for profit, but for shame and reproach” (Isaiah 30:5).

Again he laments over those from Israel as lovers of sin who have become apostates, exceedingly wicked and planning bitter things, not through God (Isaiah 30:1). For it is not right for those who wish to agree together on some evil thing to take counsel with God. But everyone who is pious and good and a lover of righteousness will take counsel with God and will go on to do what must be done. For it is written: “The thoughts of the righteous are judgments” (Proverbs 12:5).

He therefore accuses chosen Israel of bringing in, concerning Christ, a mind out of tune with God. For they deliberated, sitting in council, and indeed said: “What are we doing? For this man performs many signs. If we let him go on like this, the Romans will come and take away both your city and your country.” And another, one of those set among the leaders, says: “You know nothing at all; it is better that one man should die, and not that the whole nation should perish” (John 11:47-50).

The Lord teaches this very thing more clearly in the parables of the Gospel: “The master of the house who planted the vineyard sent his own servants to receive the fruits, but the tenants killed them” (Matthew 21:33-35). And the charges of their impiety did not stop there; for when they saw the son, sent by the father after the servants, they said among themselves, it says: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him and have his inheritance for ourselves” (Matthew 21:38).

So the authors of such bitter and unholy schemes are apostates, who add sin upon sin (Isaiah 30:1). For they killed, as I said, the holy prophets, and after them the heir himself, that is, the Son. And he tries to show that their mind had long been turned toward apostasy from God, saying: “Those who set out to go down into Egypt, but they did not ask Me, to be helped by Pharaoh and to be sheltered by the Egyptians” (Isaiah 30:2). He threw in the words “but they did not ask Me” in between.

The train of thought runs like this: Woe, he says, to those who go down into Egypt to be helped by Pharaoh and to find shelter from the Egyptians. For when war and battle had been announced to them, and the king of Assyria had taken up arms against the land of the Jews, they ran ahead to the Egyptians and called for their help. Yet they ought to have appeased God and, by turning to better ways, to have wiped away the offences by which they had struck against Him. For had they been rich in His favor, they would not have fallen under the feet of those making war…

choices.why: ταλανίζω: to call someone wretched, to grieve over them.

choices.term: ἀποστά- τας γεγονότας τοὺς ἐξ Ἰσραὴλ
choices.english: those from Israel as lovers of sin who have become apostates
choices.why: The apostates are those of Israel; they are not apostates from Israel.

choices.english: will go on to do what must be done
choices.why: πρακτέα, the things that ought to be done.
ἀπόκλητος here of Israel as the called-out people.

choices.english: a mind out of tune with God
choices.why: ἀπᾴδω is to be out of tune; the musical image is kept.
